title: Erotic massage
description: Massage of erogenous zones for sexual arousal or orgasm
wiki_lead:
Erotic massage is the use of massage techniques by one person on another person's erogenous zones for their sexual pleasure. The process may achieve or enhance the recipient's sexual excitation or arousal and sometimes achieve orgasm. The person providing the massage is called a masseur (male) or masseuse (female). Massages have been used for medical purposes for a very long time, and their use for erotic purposes also has a long history. In the case of women, the two focal areas are the abdomens and mons pubis, while in case of men, the focal areas are the male breast muscles and nipples, male genitals, the anus, and the prostate. When the massage is of a partner's genitals (manual sex), the act is usually referred to as a handjob for penises and fingering for vulvas.
Erotic massage is sometimes used as part of sex, either as foreplay, the final sex act, or as part of sex therapy. There is also a large commercial erotic massage industry, which may call their establishments massage parlours, spas, or saunas.

Commercial erotic and sexual massage

An erotic and sexual massage may be provided by independent providers or providers of broader sexual services, through erotic massage agencies, or by organized massage parlors or brothels. It takes many forms, from massage techniques that aim to integrate the sexual, spiritual, and physical, to massages with the purpose of achieving orgasm through a handjob, oral sex, or sexual intercourse.

A "happy ending" is the colloquial term for the practice of a provider offering sexual release to a client. As a result, built-up sexual tension is released, leading to a feeling of full-body relaxation and happiness at the end. The massage aiming for such an outcome is called "happy ending massage". This is sometimes offered as an addition to any other type of massage, typically in the form of a handjob. The 2009 documentary Happy Endings? follows women who worked in Asian massage parlors in Rhode Island. The film focuses on "full service" massage parlors, although "rub and tug" massage parlors (where only handjobs are offered) are also covered. Prostitution in Rhode Island was legal at the time of filming.


Legality

grok_lead: Erotic massage is a form of sensual bodywork that emphasizes stimulation of erogenous zones to induce sexual arousal, typically progressing to manual genital contact and orgasm for the recipient, distinguishing it from non-sexual therapeutic massage by its explicit erotic intent and frequent commercial provision as a paid service. Practices trace back over five millennia to ancient Asian traditions, such as those documented in Indian and Chinese texts integrating erotic touch with spiritual or healing rituals, and later in Greco-Roman bathhouses where sensual manipulations were routine for relaxation and pleasure. In contemporary contexts, it manifests in varied forms like tantric or Taoist variants focusing on energy circulation through breathing and prolonged genital mapping, or gel-based techniques such as Nuru, but remains predominantly a sexual service often evading full prostitution bans by limiting to "happy endings" via hand release. Legality diverges globally, permitted under regulated conditions in nations like Germany and the Netherlands where it aligns with legalized sex work, while prohibited or ambiguously tolerated elsewhere, frequently leading to enforcement against providers as illicit solicitation. In Japan, whose 1956 Prostitution Prevention Act covers only intercourse, establishments offering erotic massage and other non-coital services operate legally once notified to the police under the Entertainment Business Act; in the UK, selling sexual services is lawful, but a parlour where two or more people work can be prosecuted as a brothel. Defining characteristics include recipient nudity, lubricated full-body contact by a clothed or nude masseuse, and emphasis on prolonging arousal over mere relief, though empirical data on purported benefits like enhanced intimacy or stress reduction is sparse and anecdotal, overshadowed by documented risks. Notable controversies encompass health hazards for participants, including sexually transmitted infections from boundary-crossing into penetrative acts, psychological strain on providers in exploitative parlors, and associations with organized trafficking in unregulated markets, underscoring causal links between lax oversight and elevated vulnerability rather than inherent to the practice itself. Peer-reviewed inquiries highlight varied infection potentials, with low HIV transmission odds from non-penetrative elements but heightened exposure in hybrid services, prioritizing empirical caution over idealized wellness claims.
